**Sikhae (식해)** A classic Korean “raw‑fish” dish that’s actually *marinated*, not cooked. It’s a quick, refreshing appetizer or side that pairs wonderfully with steamed rice, kimchi, or a light salad. Below is a straightforward recipe that you can tweak to suit your taste or the ingredients you have on hand. --- ## 1. What You’ll Need | Category | Typical Items | Notes | |----------|---------------|-------| | **Protein** | • Fresh raw fish (mackerel, sardine, pollock, or even tuna)
• Shrimp, octopus, or scallops (optional) | Use sushi‑grade fish if you’re eating it raw. Keep everything chilled. | | **Marinade** | • Rice vinegar (or white wine vinegar) – 2 Tbsp
• Soy sauce – 2 Tbsp
• Sugar – 1 tsp (or honey)
• Salt – pinch
• Black pepper – pinch
• Garlic – 1 clove, minced
• Red pepper flakes or sliced fresh chili – ½ tsp (adjust to heat preference)
• Sesame oil – 1 tsp
• Sesame seeds – 1 tsp | The vinegar gives the “sikhae” its signature tang; adjust sweetness and saltiness to taste. | | **Garnish & Extras** | • Scallions, thinly sliced
• Cucumber, julienned
• Radish, thinly sliced
• Optional: pickled ginger, lime wedges | Adds crunch, color, and a fresh zing. | | **Tools** | • Sharp knife
• Cutting board
• Mixing bowl
• Small bowl for the sauce
• Serving dish | Keep the bowl and cutting board very clean to avoid cross‑contamination. | --- ## 2. Step‑by‑Step Instructions ### 1. Prep the Fish (or Seafood) 1. **Clean & Chill** – Rinse the fish under cold water, pat dry, and keep it on ice until you’re ready to slice. 2. **Remove Bones** – Use tweezers or a small fork to pull out any pin bones. 3. **Slice Thinly** – Cut the fish into ¼‑inch thick slices (or smaller if you prefer). A sharp knife is essential for clean cuts. > **Tip:** If you’re using shrimp or octopus, blanch them briefly in boiling water (30 s) to firm up, then cool in ice water before slicing. ### 2. Make the Marinade 1. In a small bowl, whisk together **rice vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, salt, pepper, minced garlic, red pepper flakes, and sesame oil** until the sugar dissolves. 2. Taste the sauce; it should be a balanced mix of salty, sweet, and tangy. Adjust any component slightly if needed. ### 3. Marinate 1. Place the sliced fish in a shallow dish or bowl. 2. Pour the prepared sauce over the fish, ensuring every slice is coated. 3. Gently toss to distribute the sauce evenly. 4. Cover and refrigerate for **20–30 minutes**. The fish will “cook” slightly in the acid, becoming tender and flavorful. > **Safety Note:** Because the fish is raw, keep it at 4 °C (39 °F) or below during marination. Do not leave it out at room temperature for more than 2 hours. ### 4. Garnish & Serve 1. Transfer the marinated fish to a serving platter. 2. Sprinkle with **sesame seeds** and **thinly sliced scallions**. 3. Add a few ribbons of cucumber or radish for crunch and color. 4. Serve immediately, chilled, with a side of steamed rice or a light salad. --- ## 3. Variations & Customizations | Variation | How to Adapt | |-----------|--------------| | **Vegetarian Sikhae** | Replace fish with thinly sliced cucumber, radish, or even tofu. Marinate the same way. | | **Seafood Mix** | Combine sliced fish with shrimp, octopus, and scallops for a richer flavor profile. | | **Spicy Kick** | Increase red pepper flakes or add a splash of gochujang (Korean chili paste). | | **Herbal Twist** | Add a handful of fresh cilantro or mint for a fresh herbal note. | | **Citrus Finish** | Squeeze a little lime or lemon juice over the finished dish for extra brightness. | --- ## 4. Quick Reference Table | Step | Action | Time | |------|--------|------| | 1 | Clean & slice fish | 5 min | | 2 | Whisk sauce | 2 min | | 3 | Marinate fish | 20–30 min | | 4 | Garnish & serve | 3 min | --- ### Final Thought Sikhae is all about balance—sweet, salty, tangy, and a hint of heat. Because it’s a raw dish, freshness is paramount. Keep everything chilled, use high‑quality fish, and enjoy the bright, refreshing flavors that make this Korean classic a favorite at gatherings and family meals alike. Happy cooking!
